jobs.description:
Primary Function/General Purpose Of Position

The Finance Program Manager serves as a key financial, analytical, and technical resource supporting enterprise-wide financial planning, forecasting, analytics, and value-based performance management. This role manages and coordinates complex budgeting processes; leads financial system enhancements; performs advanced financial, operational, and claims-based analytics; and delivers data-driven insights that support strategic, operational, and value-based care decision-making.

The Finance Program Manager collaborates with corporate finance, local markets, population health entities, IT/analytics teams, physicians, and senior leadership. The position independently leads long-term projects, manages financial planning applications, and communicates effectively across all levels of the organization—particularly with leaders responsible for operating budgets and value-based contract performance.

Essential Job Functions

Lead and optimize system-wide annual budget processes and quarterly reforecasts across markets, ministries, and entities.
Provide monthly close support, accounting coordination, income statements, balance sheets, and long-term financial projections.
Serve as expert and project lead for budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning.
Implement financial system enhancements, optimize workflows, and standardize tools, methodologies, dashboards, and analytics processes.
Analyze claims, eligibility, attribution, CMS/payer files, and contract datasets to identify trends, risk drivers, financial opportunities, and performance gaps.
Develop and maintain executive dashboards and KPI reporting for leadership and governance.
Support value-based contract modeling (MSSP, MA, shared savings, bundled payments) in partnership with Managed Care, Actuarial, Finance, and IT.
Provide financial, utilization, and quality analytics to support improvement initiatives, vendor reviews, and strategic decisions.
Conduct data validation, reconciliations, controls reviews, and audit preparation; collaborate with Internal Audit and external partners.
Ensure adherence to HIPAA, PHI, and organizational data governance standards.
Translate actuarial, contractual, and management guidance into actionable financial insights and strategic recommendations.
Partner with Shared Services, Market Finance, data teams, and leadership to align financial reporting, performance management processes, and compliance requirements.
Maintain strong customer-service relationships with CFOs, finance teams, and clinicians.
Prepare and deliver high-quality presentations for senior leadership, boards, committees, and external stakeholders.
Provide ad hoc analysis and proactive financial insights to support enterprise strategy and operational goals.

Company Description
Larrakia Nation Aboriginal Corporation is the peak representative body for the Larrakia peoples, dedicated to caring for Larrakia people, culture, and country. The organization plays an active role in decisions affecting Larrakia communities and land, ensuring that local voices guide services and policy. Larrakia Nation delivers a diverse range of community-based services across the Darwin region, including aged and disability care, family and cultural support, tenancy assistance, and outreach programs. The corporation also operates initiatives such as patrol services, Healthy Engagement and Assistance in the Long Grass, Return to Country, Larrakia Hosts, and Land and Sea Rangers, making it a vital provider of holistic support in the area.
Role Description
The Outreach Program Manager is responsible for overseeing the planning, delivery, and evaluation of outreach services that support Larrakia people and broader community members in Darwin, NT. This on-site role includes coordinating outreach teams, developing program plans, managing schedules, and ensuring services such as patrol, engagement in the long grass, and family support are delivered effectively and safely. The manager will work closely with community members, partner organizations, and government agencies to strengthen relationships, identify needs, and improve access to services. Day-to-day tasks include supervising staff, monitoring program budgets and reporting, maintaining accurate records, and contributing to continuous improvement of outreach models. The role also involves supporting culturally safe practices, promoting Larrakia perspectives in service design, and assisting with strategic initiatives within Larrakia Nation.

Description:

Seaford House Therapeutic Residence is seeking a Program Manager 

Lead a therapeutic residence where skilled teams help children and adolescents build safety, stability, and hope.
Seaford House is seeking an experienced, mission-driven Program Manager to lead a therapeutic residential program serving young people with behavioral and emotional needs. This is an opportunity to shape a strong trauma-informed culture, develop talented staff, and bring clinical, residential, educational, medical, and case management services together around each youth. 

Reporting to the Chief Program Officer, you will be the program’s primary operational leader—responsible for safety, service quality, staff performance, regulatory readiness, and continuous improvement. The ideal candidate combines sound clinical judgment with hands-on operational leadership and knows how to create a structured, supportive environment in which youth and staff can thrive.

As Program Manager, you will influence the full experience of Seaford House—from the quality of day-to-day care to the strength of the team delivering it. 

You will:
Build and sustain a safe, structured, trauma-informed therapeutic environment.
Coach and develop program leaders and frontline teams.
Align clinical and residential practices around individualized youth needs.
Use data, incident trends, and outcomes to improve quality and reduce risk.
Strengthen collaboration with families, funders, regulators, schools, courts, providers, and community partners.
What You’ll Lead
People and culture: Recruit, supervise, evaluate, coach, and develop Youth Advocate Supervisors, the Clinical Team Leader, and other assigned staff; promote communication, accountability, teamwork, and professional growth.
Integrated care: Coordinate clinical, residential, educational, medical, recreational, and case management services so that programming is consistent, individualized, and responsive to youth needs.
Program operations: Oversee daily operations, staffing patterns, scheduling, referrals, admissions, census, utilization, facility needs, resources, and contract performance.
Safety and crisis leadership: Support staff during crises; review serious incidents, restraints, unauthorized absences, police involvement, contraband concerns, and other significant events; ensure timely documentation, communication, reporting, and follow-up.
Quality and compliance: Maintain readiness for licensing and accreditation; oversee incident reports, corrective action plans, records, required training, certifications, audits, and regulatory or contractual reporting.
Performance improvement: Monitor program data, incident trends, youth feedback, engagement, and outcomes; identify opportunities and implement practical improvements that strengthen safety, stability, and service quality.
Community partnership: Build productive relationships with families, funders, regulators, schools, courts, providers, law enforcement, and other stakeholders.
Mission support: Participate in agency meetings, committees, court proceedings, and community activities, and step into direct service when needed.
